# S17 — Flat CSV export as a pure function (with formula-injection guard)

**Findings:** TrackerRepository.kt:230-289 (buildCsv) · **Size:** S · **Tree:** data

**Not in this slice:** the save-to-file and share flow (S43), the import flow (S44) and the backup JSON format (unchanged).

## Why

- The CSV interleaves `tracker` and `entry` record rows with 18 mostly blank columns and blank separator lines. It includes soft-deleted entries and prints YES_NO values as `1.0`, so it opens badly in a spreadsheet.
- Text cells that begin with `=`, `+`, `-` or `@` are treated as formulas by spreadsheet programs. A tracker name or note such as `=HYPERLINK(...)` would run when the user opens their own export.
- The builder is private to the repository and cannot be unit tested without Android.

## Files

- New `app/src/main/java/com/squalor/consecutor/CsvExport.kt`
- New `app/src/test/java/com/squalor/consecutor/CsvExportTest.kt`
- `app/src/main/java/com/squalor/consecutor/TrackerRepository.kt` (remove `buildCsv` and `csv`; `exportCsv` calls `CsvExport.build`)

## Failing tests

JVM, in `CsvExportTest`:
- `header is date,tracker,type,value,unit,note`
- `one row per active entry with tracker name, type and unit` (deleted entries are not exported)
- `yes_no value is 1 and count values have no trailing zeros` (`3.0` is `3`, `2.5` is `2.5`, never `1.0E10`)
- `measure entry without a value gives an empty value cell`
- `quotes cells with commas, quotes and line breaks, doubling inner quotes`
- `prefixes text cells that start with = + - @ tab or carriage return with a single quote`
- `does not prefix numeric value cells, so a negative measure stays -5`
- `rows are ordered by tracker id then date`
- `no trackers gives the header only`

## Implement

1. `object CsvExport { fun build(bundles: List<TrackerBundle>): String }` (no Android imports).
2. Columns, in order: `date` (the entry's `effectiveDate`, ISO), `tracker` (name), `type` (`YES_NO`, `COUNT`, `MEASURE`), `value`, `unit`, `note`. Archived trackers are included. Soft-deleted entries are not.
3. Value cell: YES_NO is `1`. Otherwise format the double with `BigDecimal(value.toString()).stripTrailingZeros().toPlainString()` so there is no scientific notation and the decimal separator is always `.`, whatever the locale. Null (MEASURE without a value) is empty.
4. Text cells (`tracker`, `unit`, `note`): if the text starts with `=`, `+`, `-`, `@`, a tab or a carriage return, prefix a single quote `'`. Then, if it contains a comma, double quote, `\r` or `\n`, wrap it in double quotes and double any inner quotes (RFC 4180). The value, date and type cells are never prefixed.
5. Lines end with `\r\n`, including the last one. Use UTF-8 without a byte-order mark.
6. In the repository delete `buildCsv` and `csv`, and make `exportCsv(context)` write `CsvExport.build(trackerDao.getTrackerBundles())` to the same cache file it uses today. (S43 later replaces the file handling.)
7. Update the "CSV export formatting" bullet in `DEVELOPERS.md`'s testing strategy to point at `CsvExportTest`.

## Check

- `./gradlew testDebugUnitTest` passes.
- Manual: export a CSV from a debug build with a tracker named `=1+1` and a note with a comma and a line break. Open it in LibreOffice Calc (or any spreadsheet). The name cell shows the text `'=1+1` (the leading quote is visible, and no formula runs), and the note stays in one cell.
